data.text: Stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Use acetaminophen instead if needed, and start magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights because your previous magnesium trend has been low-normal.

prior_context.speaker: nurse_jamison
prior_context.text: I am placing orders for CBC, BMP, magnesium, TSH, and a repeat ECG before Dr. Patel comes in.

prior_context.speaker: labtech_mira
prior_context.text: I have the tubes labeled. Marcus, I am drawing blood now and the results should be back before the cardiologist finalizes the plan.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Thanks. Please use the cell first for any result callbacks unless that fails.

prior_context.speaker: labtech_mira

prior_context.speaker: nurse_jamison
prior_context.text: Your sister asked at the desk whether the timing changed. I told her only that you are still being evaluated and we have not set the final arrival time.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: That is exactly what I want. She can know the times later, not the reason anything changes.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Hi Marcus, I reviewed the emergency-department tracing and today's ECG. You are still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, but you are stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Is cardioversion still the plan, or are we trying to just slow the rate?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Cardioversion is still the plan. Based on what we know so far, we were aiming for Wednesday morning, but I want the lab results and the medication history fully reconciled first.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Until then, continue apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily without interruption. Increase metoprolol tartrate from 25 milligrams twice daily to 37.5 milligrams twice daily starting tonight.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control, aiming for Wednesday morning, pending lab results and full medication history reconciliation before the cardiologist finalizes the plan. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active. As of the latest update, Marcus is still being evaluated and no final arrival time has been set; Nina asked at the desk whether the timing changed, and Jamison told her only that Marcus is still being evaluated with no final arrival time set.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list for review. As part of this review, Nurse Jamison asked Marcus whether he has taken anything over the counter for pain or colds; Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before he remembered he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Nurse Jamison says they will likely tell Marcus to stop ibuprofen because it raises bleeding risk with apixaban, and ibuprofen use should be flagged for medication review. Nurse Jamison also asked Marcus whether he has missed any doses of apixaban in the last month and whether there were any completely missed doses in the last three weeks; Marcus reported he has not missed any morning doses, reports no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers, and although he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations, he still took that pill before bed. Marcus also recalls that before cardioversion they were strict about not missing apixaban doses. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Nurse Jamison further asked Marcus about alcohol, supplements, or stimulants that could affect rhythm; Marcus answered that he does not drink energy drinks. Flag for medication review.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
